statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of the UK redirect destination.

paths.description: UK homepage and global navigation; represents entry, campaigns, consent and recommendations.
All smartphones listing; represents category discovery, filtering and product cards.
Galaxy S26 Ultra detail; represents long-form product storytelling, media and specifications.
Galaxy S26 Ultra buying tool; represents the primary commercial selection journey through device, storage, colour, trade-in and payment options.

findings.summary: Homepage loading performance is poor
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 18.5 s, Speed Index 8.9 s and TBT 370 ms; the independent trace measured LCP 2.56 s, confirming substantial run variability and a fragile load path.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, reduce early script/style work, and validate against lab and field Core Web Vitals.

findings.summary: Consent modal obscures every primary page on first load
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots of the home and buy paths show a large modal and dimmed page blocking the main content before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the initial consent surface, preserve equally prominent accept/decline choices, and avoid obscuring the full primary experience.

findings.summary: Major mobile layout shifts occur on key templates
findings.evidence: The layout primitive measured CLS 0.229 on home, 0.684 on listing and 0.305 on buy; only the product detail was stable at 0.0008.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late UI, consent and product modules; add intrinsic dimensions and stable font fallbacks.

findings.summary: Long main-thread tasks delay interaction
findings.evidence: Mobile captures recorded tasks up to 426 ms on home, 395 ms on listing and 579 ms on buy; Lighthouse measured 370 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Split and defer component initialization, reduce third-party execution, and schedule non-critical work after interaction readiness.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is heavy and render-blocking
findings.evidence: HAR captured 3.69 MB across 93 requests, 13 stylesheets and many parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority CSS candidates; several fonts lack cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, cache fonts, remove duplicate font origins and prioritise only the true LCP resource.

findings.summary: Some controls and images lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name and image-alt audits; the image primitive reported 74 of 100 img elements without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable control an accessible name and provide meaningful alt or explicit decorative empty alt.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions at scale
findings.evidence: The image primitive found all 100 sampled images missing width and height attributes, aligning with high CLS on three templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio for image slots before lazy content arrives.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP and X-Content-Type-Options are missing; six of eight cookies lack Secure and several use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP and nosniff, and mark all cookies Secure with the narrowest viable SameSite/HttpOnly settings.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS and SAMEORIGIN framing protection, but omit CSP, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors, a strict Referrer-Policy, a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and nosniff.

findings.summary: Homepage asset payload is disproportionate
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 3.69 MB, led by a 1.06 MB autoplay MP4, an 836 KB SVG sprite and duplicate font files from two origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace/defer decorative video, subset the SVG sprite and fonts, and remove duplicate asset origins.

findings.summary: Third-party and media costs dominate the load
findings.evidence: Third-party origins account for 2.87 MB of 3.69 MB transferred, and the autoplay hero MP4 alone transfers 1.06 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit third-party/media budgets, load the hero video on intent or suitable conditions, and gate vendors behind consent.

findings.summary: No user-driven dark colour scheme
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot remains the same light presentation and the computed root color-scheme is normal; CSS inspection found no dark-mode adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide prefers-color-scheme-driven surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference does not suppress motion
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, five animations were still running (500–1500 ms), while CSS inspection found no reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce branch that removes non-essential transitions and auto-advance.

findings.summary: Overlay-heavy UI does not expose native dialog/popover primitives
findings.evidence: The visible consent overlay and popup-heavy buying experience are present, while probes report zero dialog, popover and details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal flows with dialog and transient UI with popover, including native focus management and light dismiss.

findings.summary: Persistent consent and chat chrome competes with product content
findings.evidence: Screenshots show a full blocking consent panel plus a floating WhatsApp control over the product and purchase surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent overlays and reserve floating chrome for user-invoked support.

findings.summary: Unused and duplicated payload inflates the load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 211 KiB unused JavaScript and 44 KiB unused CSS; HAR shows duplicate SamsungOne fonts served from two origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split template bundles, remove duplicate font delivery and gate third-party modules behind need or consent.

findings.summary: Primary content lacks a main landmark
findings.evidence: All four template probes report zero main elements, although skip links and visible dotted focus are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the primary page content in main and retain the existing skip-link and focus visibility behaviour.

findings.summary: The page emits browser console errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the errors-in-console audit on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove uncaught runtime and resource errors, and keep production console output clean.

findings.summary: JavaScript pseudo-links replace real platform controls
findings.evidence: Probes counted 11 javascript: links on home, 19 on listing and 91 on buy, while Lighthouse failed crawlable anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions and real href links for navigation; remove javascript: and javascript:void anchors.

findings.summary: Action links are not consistently crawlable
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable anchors and link-name; DOM probes found up to 91 javascript: links on the purchase page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use descriptive real links for navigation and buttons for in-page actions.

findings.summary: Third-party footprint is large before consent choice
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 66 third-party requests and 2.87 MB from third-party origins, including Adobe DTM and TrustArc; trackers probe found 11 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential vendors until consent, remove unused integrations and batch/minimise analytics.

findings.summary: Consent choice blocks content and uses attention-heavy framing
findings.evidence: The first-load modal prevents access to the page until Configure, Accept All or Decline All is chosen, rather than allowing the content to remain usable.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep consent controls honest and equivalent while allowing non-essential-content browsing without a full-screen interruption.

findings.summary: Early network and script work is excessive
findings.evidence: The homepage performs 93 requests with 30 scripts, while mobile captures record 426 ms of single-task work and Lighthouse reports substantial unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer recommendations, analytics and below-fold components until idle, visibility or user intent.

findings.summary: Initial DOM and heap footprint is large
findings.evidence: The homepage baseline heap contained 354,535 nodes and 23.45 MB self size before meaningful interaction, high for a retail landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce pre-rendered hidden UI, unload dormant components and cap caches/observers.

findings.summary: No explicit high-contrast adaptation
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across representative pages found color-scheme normal and no preference-oriented rules; the interface relies on fixed colours rather than explicit forced-colors/prefers-contrast support.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for controls, borders and custom scroll affordances.

findings.summary: Route and state changes omit View Transitions
findings.evidence: CSS inspection on all four templates found zero view-transition rules despite navigation and buying-tool state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route and buying-tool state changes, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long product storytelling does not use declarative scroll timelines
findings.evidence: The 41,375 px product page contains rich storytelling but CSS inspection found zero animation-timeline or scroll-timeline rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Move any scroll-linked reveals or progress effects to CSS scroll-driven animations.

findings.summary: Long pages lack declarative scroll-state-aware chrome
findings.evidence: The product page is 41,375 px tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state container queries or scroll timelines for progress/orientation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware header treatment on long product pages.

findings.summary: Menus and overlays use custom positioning instead of anchor positioning
findings.evidence: The site exposes navigation, filters and popup controls, but CSS inspection found zero anchor-name or position-anchor declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for transient menus and tooltips.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport layout rather than container queries
findings.evidence: CSS inspection on home, listing, product and buy templates found zero @container rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reused cards, product selectors and recommendation modules.

findings.summary: Public account entry exposes no passkey affordance
findings.evidence: The public templates expose Sign In/Sign-Up but DOM/CSS probes found no WebAuthn/passkey affordance; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys in Samsung account sign-in and request any browser permissions only after a user action.

findings.summary: Commerce capability is not exposed as structured agent tools
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored 0.67 and probes found no WebMCP or agentic form/tool registration despite a structured product-buying journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped, user-confirmed product comparison and basket actions through WebMCP/agentic forms.
